title: The E. coli K-12 Reference Genome: NC_000913.3 (MG1655)
description: The E. coli K-12 reference genome (Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655, assembly NC_000913.3 (MG1655)) spans approximately 4.64 Mb across 1 circular chromosome chromosomes, encoding approx 4,300 protein-coding genes (estimate). This record is the assembly-level overview: the anchor for the deterministic scale chromosome -> gene -> protein product -> pathway -> trait used across this database. REFERENCE GENOME ONLY: a public consensus assembly, never any real person's private genetic data.
how_it_works: Genome assembly stitches long sequencing reads into chromosome-scale scaffolds, annotates genes by homology and experiment, and publishes the consensus coordinates everyone references. All records in this database hang off these coordinates deterministically.
key_points: Assembly NC_000913.3 (MG1655): the public reference coordinates.
standards: Coordinates follow the named assembly NC_000913.3 (MG1655)
Numeric values are approximate unless stated; estimates are labeled

title: E. coli K-12 Chromosome circular (NC_000913.3 (MG1655))
description: Chromosome circular of the E. coli K-12 reference genome (assembly NC_000913.3 (MG1655)). Each chromosome is a deterministic address space: genes live at fixed coordinates on it, so gene -> protein -> pathway -> trait records resolve unambiguously. Sizes here are approximate (labeled estimates).
how_it_works: Chromosomes package DNA with histones into chromatin; genes are transcribed from fixed loci. The demo computes this chromosome's approximate share of the whole genome.
key_points: Deterministic address space for genes at fixed coordinates.
Part of the 1 circular chromosome set in assembly NC_000913.3 (MG1655).

title: E. coli K-12: The Deterministic Scale Ladder
description: The Deterministic Scale Ladder (E. coli K-12). chromosome -> gene -> protein product -> pathway -> trait: each level is a deterministic function of the level below in the reference assembly. No level is a sample or a guess; the ladder is the database's spine.
how_it_works: Scaling walks the ladder deterministically: pick a level, apply its rules, land on the next level. The generator ladder ranks are simple -> most competitive -> mix-and-match -> unmade -> top-notch -> future grade -> god mode.
key_points: Deterministic: same level, same rules, same result.
Generator bound: stops at 10^15 records or complete-with-reason.
standards: Scaling claims are structural, not empirical, and labeled as such
citations: JAH Databases genome lane design notes
